idea: Signs of a hidden water leak
title: Detecting Hidden Water Leaks Using the Water Meter Indicator
description: An educational guide explaining how to use a water meter's low-flow indicator dial to confirm active, hidden leaks in pressurized supply piping.
image_prompt: A sharp, professional vertical 9:16 high-detail photograph of a clean brass analog water meter installed on an exposed domestic supply line. The camera focuses closely at a 45-degree overhead angle onto the clear glass face of the meter register. Visible on the meter face are clear black numbers, a primary red sweep hand, and a small, distinct red triangular low-flow indicator wheel in the center. The meter is connected via heavy brass threaded fittings to clean copper piping. The background is a soft-focus clean concrete utility wall with smooth ambient lighting. The top and bottom thirds of the vertical composition are clean and uncluttered. No text, no visual overlays, no logos, no watermarks, realistic plumbing geometry and physical details.
visual_story: The visual focuses on the register face of a physical water meter, specifically highlighting the small low-flow indicator wheel (often shaped like a triangle or star). By providing a clean, realistic view of the meter's internal dial setup, the visual teaches viewers what specific component to observe when diagnosing an invisible leak. The clear space around the meter allows key educational points to be placed without obscuring the brass fittings or dial display.

on_image_text.hook: Confirm Hidden Leaks Without Opening Walls
on_image_text.explanation: The small triangular wheel on your water meter spins whenever water moves through the main line.
on_image_text.takeaway: Shut off all fixtures. If this indicator still rotates, you have an active supply leak.
